purpose: A versioned, attributed ingredient research queue for the DermaSynth FYP. It records actual ingredient names, source roles, and evidence boundaries without selecting ingredients for a routine.
governance: This knowledge base is for a non-commercial academic study and is not a product catalogue, treatment protocol, dosing guide, or suitability engine.
CIR records are safety-provenance citations only; no report text, conclusion, table, figure, or embedding is stored here.
EWG Skin Deep is an external hazard-context link only. No scores, ratings, product records, or database fields are copied into this knowledge base.
Medical-journal records are attributed review notes. They remain outside Pinecone until a qualified reviewer approves the claim scope and the upload gate is satisfied.
No record in this file may unlock a named ingredient, product, concentration, frequency, combination, or treatment claim in a routine.

sourceRecords.title: A Double-Blind, Randomized Clinical Trial of Niacinamide 4% versus Hydroquinone 4% in the Treatment of Melasma
sourceRecords.reuseNote: A short attributed research note may be reviewed under the displayed CC BY licence; preserve the citation and licence when used.
sourceRecords.claimBoundary: A small, short, disease-specific split-face study with sunscreen co-use and no vehicle comparator cannot establish a general uneven-tone outcome, suitability, strength, or routine instruction.

sourceRecords.title: Comparison of Topical 5% Nicotinamide Gel versus 2% Clindamycin Gel in the Treatment of Mild to Moderate Acne Vulgaris
sourceRecords.publisher: Journal of Research in Medical Sciences
sourceRecords.reuseNote: This FYP-only research note must remain non-commercial and attributed. Reassess rights before a billed or public product deployment.
sourceRecords.claimBoundary: A short, single-site active-comparator study in female participants with clinical acne cannot become a consumer acne recommendation, a dose rule, or a substitute for clinical care.

sourceRecords.title: Efficacy of a Cream Containing Ceramides and Magnesium in the Treatment of Mild to Moderate Atopic Dermatitis: A Randomized, Double-Blind, Emollient- and Hydrocortisone-Controlled Trial
sourceRecords.reuseNote: This FYP-only research note must remain non-commercial and attributed. It documents formulation context, not a component-level effect estimate.
sourceRecords.claimBoundary: The study evaluated a multi-ingredient formulation in adults with atopic dermatitis; its effects cannot be assigned to ceramides, cholesterol, glycerol, or any one component.

sourceRecords.title: Performance and Tolerability of a New Topical Dexpanthenol-Containing Emollient Line in Subjects with Dry Skin and Sensitive Skin
sourceRecords.reuseNote: A short attributed research note may be reviewed under the displayed CC BY licence; retain the stated funding and formulation limits.
sourceRecords.claimBoundary: These studies examined a sponsor-provided multi-ingredient emollient line in healthy adults without a placebo formulation; they cannot establish an effect for dexpanthenol, glycerin, or niacinamide alone.

sourceRecords.title: A Double-Blinded, Randomized, Vehicle-Controlled Study of the Efficacy of a Moisturizer Containing Licochalcone A, 1,2-Decanediol, L-Carnitine, and Salicylic Acid in Maintaining Acne Improvement
